steps.intent: Initialize the authenticated Archer command without navigating to an unvalidated destination.

steps.userPrompt:
Write every user-facing status, question, or explanation in English. Never invent footage content, dialogue, or events that are not present in the supplied source file -- you are editing real, user-approved footage only, not generating new video.

Setup: the video-use skill is already cloned into your Claude Code skills directory by the platform -- do not clone it again. Read its SKILL.md and reference docs (including skills/manim-video/SKILL.md if you end up building a Manim animation) before editing anything. Confirm ELEVENLABS_API_KEY is present in the environment before transcribing; if it is missing, stop and report that clearly instead of guessing or fabricating a key. All session outputs belong in edit/ next to the source footage, per video-use's own layout -- never write inside the video-use skill directory itself.

Download the real source footage from {{context.intakeContext.footage_url}} into your working directory -- if this value is blank, stop immediately and report that no footage URL was supplied rather than guessing one.

PHASE 1 -- INVENTORY AND PROPOSE (always do this first):
1. ffprobe the source file. Transcribe it (ElevenLabs Scribe, word-level timestamps, verbatim -- never phrase-level, never normalized fillers). Cache the transcript; never re-transcribe the same source later in this session.
2. Pack the transcript into a phrase-level reading view (break on silence >= 0.5s or speaker change) -- this is what you reason from, not raw JSON.
3. Pre-scan for problems: note verbal slips, false starts, or phrasings to avoid.
4. Sample one or two visual timeline views (filmstrip + waveform) for a first impression of the footage.
5. Propose a strategy in 4-8 plain-English sentences: shape/structure, which moments to keep, cut direction, animation plan (if any -- ask what engine/style if it's not obvious: HyperFrames for web-native motion, Remotion for React compositions, Manim for diagrams/equations, PIL+ffmpeg for simple overlay cards), grade direction, subtitle style (default: two-word uppercase chunks, speech-synced, unless the footage calls for a calmer natural-sentence style), and a rough length estimate. Ask any clarifying questions you genuinely need answered as part of this same message -- you only get one round of confirmation before executing, so ask everything now (palette/font/brand direction for animations, must-keep or must-cut moments, target aspect ratio) rather than assuming defaults you're not confident about.
6. Write this proposal as plain text to /home/user/edit/pending_confirmation.txt and stop there. Do not touch the cut, do not render anything, do not produce a final file this turn. The platform will pause here and bring the user's reply back to you in a later turn -- when that happens the reply text (approval, answers to your questions, or requested changes) will be provided to you automatically before this same prompt runs again; proceed directly to Phase 2 using it instead of re-proposing.

PHASE 2 -- EXECUTE (only once a confirmation reply has actually been provided to you; never do this on the same turn as Phase 1):
1. Build edl.json: pick the best take of each beat and assemble chronologically by beat (not by source clip order). Start/end times must fall on word boundaries from the transcript; pad every cut edge 30-200ms (Scribe timestamps drift 50-100ms, padding absorbs it); prefer silences >= 400ms as cut targets; extend past laughs/punchlines/emphasis beats rather than cutting them tight. If a beat needs picking from many takes, delegate that selection to a sub-agent via the Agent tool with a self-contained brief (packed transcript, content/narrative context, target runtime, verbal slips to avoid) rather than trying to hold all the takes in your own reasoning at once.
2. If the strategy calls for animations, build every animation slot in a separate PARALLEL sub-agent -- spawn all of them at once via the Agent tool, never sequentially (total wall time should be about as long as the single slowest animation, not the sum of all of them). Each sub-agent's brief must be fully self-contained (sub-agents share no context with you or each other): one-sentence goal, absolute output path (edit/animations/slot_<id>/render.mp4), exact technical spec (resolution/fps/codec/duration), the palette/font/style you settled on in Phase 1 as concrete values, a frame-by-frame timeline with cubic easing (never linear), an anti-list of what NOT to add, and an instruction to pick the most obvious interpretation of anything ambiguous rather than asking you a question back. One sub-agent produces exactly one file so parallel agents never collide.
3. Apply color grade per-segment during extraction (not after concat, which would double-encode).
4. Render: per-segment extract with 30ms audio fades at every cut, lossless concat, then overlays (using setpts=PTS-STARTPTS+T/TB so each overlay's frame 0 lands at its window start), then subtitles burned in LAST -- subtitles applied before overlays would be hidden behind them. Master subtitle timing must use output-timeline offsets (output_time = word.start - segment_start + segment_offset), not source-clip time. Do a fast preview-resolution pass first.
5. Self-evaluate the rendered output (not the sources) before showing anyone the result: sample the rendered file at every cut boundary (+/-1.5s) and check for visual discontinuity, an audio pop that slipped past the fade, a subtitle hidden behind an overlay, or a misaligned/wrong-frame overlay; also sample the first 2s, last 2s, and a couple of midpoints for grade consistency and subtitle readability; confirm total duration matches the EDL. Fix and re-render anything that fails, up to 3 self-eval passes -- if issues remain after that, finish anyway and describe them honestly in your final message rather than looping forever.
6. Append a session entry to edit/project.md (strategy, decisions with one-line reasoning, outstanding items) so a future session on this same footage can pick up where this one left off.
7. Write the final rendered file to BOTH edit/final.mp4 (video-use's own convention) AND /home/user/output/final.mp4 exactly (create the directory if needed) -- the second path is what the platform reads back after you finish; do not use any other path or filename for it.
8. In your final message, state the output path, a one-paragraph summary of what was cut/graded/captioned/animated, and any step that failed or was skipped and why.

Hard rules, non-negotiable regardless of what else you do: subtitles always burn in last, after every overlay. Extract-then-concat losslessly, never a single-pass filtergraph once overlays exist. 30ms audio fades at every cut. Overlays always use the setpts shift described above. Master subtitle timing always uses output-timeline offsets. Never cut inside a word. Cut padding always 30-200ms. Transcription is always word-level verbatim, never phrase-level or filler-normalized. Never re-transcribe a cached source. Animations for multiple slots are always parallel sub-agents, never sequential.

commitMessage: Full video-use parity: cut/edit selection, grading, subtitles, parallel-sub-agent animations, self-eval, strategy confirmation, project memory
